- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and overpredicts continuation — reduce forecast peak by 5-10% and smooth out the slope.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–0.3), model frequently underestimates upward momentum — raise forecast mean by 1–2% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is flat or mildly negative — apply a +1.5–2.5% bias to first 5–7 days of forecast.
- When sentiment shows strong negative trend (e.g., -0.4+ for 3+ days), model often fails to anticipate reversal — add a +0.5–1.0% upward bias in final 5–7 days to capture mean reversion.
- Model tends to lag in predicting true price by 1–3 days — shift forecast 1–2 days ahead by +0.5–1.0% to account for lagged sentiment-driven momentum.
